Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 4722 of 2023

Revisionist :- Rukmuddin
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Revisionist :- Radha Mohan Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra,J.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent and perused
the material available on record.

As per office report dated 08.01.2025, which is based on communication received from CJM,
concerned.
Notice is personally served upon the respondent No.2, but none appeared on behalf of respondent No.2 as yet.

Instant Criminal Revision has been filed by the revisionist against the judgment and order 23.06.2023 passed Principal Judge, Family Court, Bulandshahar in Maintenance Case No.481 of 2022, under Section 125 Cr.P.C.

By the impugned order learned court below has award maintenance to the tune to Rs.4,000/- per month from the date of filing of application bearing dated 26.04.2022 to the applicant/respondent No.2 which is payable by the revisionist/husband.

sentences.text: The factual matrix of the case in brief is that respondent No.2 filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. seeking maintenance form her husband/opposite party at the rate of Rs.20,000/- per month.
She has averred in the application that her marriage with opposite party was solemnized according to muslim rites and rituals on 20.03.2020.
Her father gave sufficient gifts and dowries in the marriage and he spent around Rs.10 lakh as dowry in the marriage of the parties.

However,
husband and in-laws are not satisfied from the dowry received in the marriage and they started demanding Rs.3 lakh as additional dowry to purchase a four wheeler and when their demand was not fulfilled they started harassing and torturing her.

On 04.01.2021 she was turned out from her matrimonial home in her wearing apparel and was threatened that unless she come back with Rs.3 lakh in cash, she would not be permitted to live at their place.
She lodged an FIR under Section 498A,323, 506 IPC read with section of D.P. Act, P.S. Chhatari District Bulandshahar.
Nevertheless the opposite party and his family members did not relent and they sticked to their demand of dowry and the opposite party deserted her.

Applicant is not having any independent source of income,
opposite party is a evil bodied persons.
He is also having agricultural land, he sells buffalow milk and earns around Rs.50,000/- per month from all sources.

Opposite party appeared in reply to summons and filed his reply 14(A)(1) before the court below, in which he admitted factum of marriage, but averred that the attitude of the applicant was very objectionable.
She denied the opposite party of matrimonial bliss and deprived him from cohabitation with her which is a necessary of concomitant of marriage and ultimately she refused to live with him.
No demand of dowry was ever made as alleged by the applicant.

The marriage was solemnized without taking dowry, the opposite party is a labourer and he is ready to keep the applicant with him and for that purpose he is ready to file an under taking also before the court.

The learned court below framed as many as six issues on the basis of pleadings of the parties and at the stage of evidence applicant appeared as a witness and to controvert the evidence of applicant,
opposite party appeared in witness box as PW-1.

The learned court below after appreciating the evidence on record gave a finding that applicant is legally married wife of the opposite party, she is living separately from opposite party with sufficient reasons and cause, opposite party has neglected to maintain the applicant and he never provided maintenance to her from the period when she started living separately from her.

The applicant is unable to maintain herself, although the applicant has failed to prove any satisfactory evidence in support of his version that opposite party earns around Rs.50,000/- per month from different sources, but even if it is assumed that opposite party is a labourer as per his own stand.

In the present case itself a labourer can also earn around Rs.400/- per day and he is under obligation to maintain his estranged wife and with these finding the court below as awarded maintenance Rs.4,000/- per month from the date of filing of application.

Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the learned court below has assumed the daily income of the revisionist as Rs.400/-, but the court below failed to realized the fact that it is not necessary that applicant will get job on each and every day of month and for a substantial period of monthly, he remained jobless.
Thus it cannot be assumed that revisionist gets Rs.12,000/- per month and on that count the quantum of maintenance is excessive and and beyond the financial capacity of the revisionist.

sentences.text: 2 There is no evidence on record that he is employed any where from where her derived some fixed income.
There is also not any evidence in support of the fact that he is possessed immovable property as claimed by the applicant, because there is no evidence in support of this version of the applicant.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. submitted that the amount of maintenance is awarded Rs.4,000/- per month as it is a very paltry amount for maintenance for a women who has to take shelter at a parental home being subjected to matrimonial cruelty by her husband.

On perusal of material on record it appears that the learned court below has placed reliance on judgment of Hon?ble Supreme Court in Shailja and another Vs. Khobbanna (2018) 12 SCC 199 the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that:-
"Merely because the wife is capable of earning it would not be a sufficient ground to reduce the maintenance awarded by the Family Court.

entities.text: Shailja and another Vs. Khobbanna (2018) 12 SCC 199
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court has to determine whether the income of the wife is sufficient to enable her to maintain herself, in accordance with the lifestyle of her husband in the matrimonial home sustenance does not mean, and can not be allowed to mean mere survival."

Learned court below has also placed reliance on Sunita Kachwaha and others Vs. Anil Kachwaha 2014 (16) SCC 316 , wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that:-
"The wife had a postgraduate degree and was employed as a teacher in Jabalpur.

entities.text: Sunita Kachwaha and others Vs. Anil Kachwaha 2014 (16) SCC 316
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The husband raised a contention that since the wife had sufficient income, She would not require financial assistance from the husband.
The Supreme Court replied this contention and held that merely because the wife was earning some income, it could not be a ground to reject her claim for maintenance."
In the present case, there is no independent income of the respondent No.2.

Similarly there is no proof of any fixed income of the respondent No.2, therefore, learned court blow has rightly delved on premises that as the opposite has claimed himself as a labourer, he is being a evil bodied person her derives daily income of Rs.400/-.

However, there is no submission for counsel for the revisionist that it is not necessary that a labourer gets some labour work on each and every day of the month, therefore impugned judgment deserves to be upheld with slight modification as under.

The amount of maintenance awarded in the impugned order is modified to the extent that revisionist husband will pay Rs.3,000- per month to the applicant/ respondent No.2 from the date of filing of application dated 26.04.2022 to date of judgment dated 23.06.2023 and thereafter he will pay Rs.4,000- per month to the applicant as maintenance.
The revision stands disposed of with this modification.
